fear noun

classical

Traupman 152

metus, metūs m.

noun, fourth declension

fear, dread

The general word, fear of what is coming. For being afraid see timēre.

Other words

  • timor, timōris m. — fear, alarm

    noun, third declension · also used · classical · Cic. Tusc. 4.19 (Lewis & Short)

    Fear of a danger close at hand: Cicero defines it as metum malī appropinquantis.

  • terror, terrōris m. — terror, great fear

    noun, third declension · also used · classical · Cic. Tusc. 4.19 (Lewis & Short); Andresian p. 36; Traupman 158

    Fear that shakes one, with pallor and chattering teeth (Cic. Tusc. 4.19).

  • pavor, pavōris m. — panic, trembling fear

    noun, third declension · also used · classical · Lewis & Short, s.v. pavor

  • formīdō, formīdāre, formīdāvī, formīdātum — dread, be terrified of

    verb, first conjugation · also used · classical · Plaut. Capt. 4.4.5: illum (Lewis & Short s.v. formīdō); Traupman 306

Examples

  • Cūrāvit ut illīs Juppiter īrātus esset.

    He put the fear of God into them.Traupman 314

  • prae metū

    out of fearTraupman 314

  • propter metum

    out of fearTraupman 355

See also be afraid, scared to death, anxiety.
